verified_facts_vs_interpretation.verified: both contestants, under their default read configurations and the bounded 1+1 budget, were served the same WeChat anti-bot verification page and extracted 0/4 objective fields; the challenger staged successfully (0.9.3) and its tool run succeeded mechanically; the pre-match baseline shows the page is fetchable with a plain browser-UA HTTP client
verified_facts_vs_interpretation.interpretation: the block is automation-fingerprint-based; the challenger's default headless chromium presents a worse-or-equal fingerprint to the native fetcher on this surface; crawl4ai remains operationally validated as a tool (staged, ran, produced structured output) but demonstrated no extraction advantage on the tested ownership question at materially higher cost

outcome_rationale: On the tested ownership question (complex-web.read escalation), Crawl4AI is operational but showed no quality advantage over the incumbent on the real case - both were identically blocked by the same anti-bot surface - while adding a ~1.59GB ephemeral footprint, staging friction, and a heavyweight runtime lifecycle. Per Arena v0.2, REJECT_CHALLENGER means it should not remain an active challenger for THIS ownership question; as a capable loser it stays eligible for a future scenario-specific re-challenge (e.g., with explicitly authorized anti-detection configuration) without any production install.
scope_limits: one real case, one runtime, default configurations, bounded 1+1 attempts; this decision makes no claim about Crawl4AI's general web-extraction superiority or JS-heavy non-anti-bot pages
routing_impact: none: complex-web.read remains AVAILABLE_WITH_SCOPE under the native DEGRADED path; the observed extraction fallback remains web_reader (TASK-002 P7, which DID read this exact page). No adapter or source-ownership change.
